stories.headline: Stripe agrees to buy AI model gateway OpenRouter for about $7.5B, its largest deal ever

key_facts.fact: Stripe announced on August 19 that it agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a gateway that routes and optimizes token usage across more than 400 models from over 80 providers.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe, the programmable financial services company, today announced that it has agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a leading AI model gateway and routing platform. OpenRouter helps businesses route and optimize token usage across 400+ models from more than 80 providers.

key_facts.fact: Terms were not disclosed, but the New York Times put the price at about $7.5 billion, with $1.5 billion going to OpenRouter's founders and $6 billion to investors.
key_facts.excerpt: While the company didn't disclose the deal price, sources told the New York Times that it paid $7.5 billion... the founders alone will reportedly receive $1.5 billion from the sale... Investors will get the remaining $6 billion, according to the NYT.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter raised a $113 million round at roughly a $1.3 billion valuation less than three months earlier, in May 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Less than three months ago OpenRouter raised $113 million at a valuation of of about $1.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison said the deal will let businesses 'maximize profitability by routing their requests intelligently and spending their tokens efficiently'.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal will "maximize profitability by routing their requests intelligently and spending their tokens efficiently," Stripe CEO Patrick Collison said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: A leaked letter from Stripe's founders to investors justified the deal by saying they decided January 1 marked 'the beginning of the singularity' and have been operating on that basis.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's a fuzzy and perhaps already overworked term but we decided that January 1 marked the beginning of the singularity and we've been operating on that basis," they wrote in the letter, published by Eric Newcomer and verified by TechCrunch.

key_facts.fact: Stripe reportedly had to outbid other interested buyers including Databricks; Stripe says 88% of the Forbes AI 50, including OpenAI and Anthropic, use its products.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe reportedly had to outbid others interested in the fast-growing startup, including Databricks... Stripe says that 88% of the Forbes AI 50 are using its products, including OpenAI and Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter said it will keep operating independently after the deal closes in a few weeks, with its 'product, mission, and current commitments' unchanged.
key_facts.excerpt: It seems as if OpenRouter will continue to operate independently after the deal closes in a few weeks, or so the startup promised in its own blog post, saying that its "product, mission, and current commitments remain unchanged."

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO tells staff the company 'will be a public company in 2027', maybe sooner

key_facts.fact: At an all-hands on Wednesday, August 19, CFO Sarah Friar told OpenAI employees the lab 'will be a public company in 2027', and could debut sooner if 'our business continues to inflect'.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told employees during an all-hands meeting on Wednesday that the artificial intelligence lab "will be a public company in 2027," but that it could make its public market debut sooner if "our business continues to inflect."

key_facts.fact: Friar framed the listing as a fundraise rather than an endpoint: 'The IPO is not a finish line, it is a milestone, another fundraise. We raised $122 billion in March, and that gives us flexibility.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The IPO is not a finish line, it is a milestone, another fundraise," Friar told employees... "We raised $122 billion in March, and that gives us flexibility."

key_facts.fact: She told staff not to worry if Anthropic lists first: 'There is a chance they pull the cover off that confidential file in the coming weeks and become public in September. That's OK, we are running our own race.'
key_facts.excerpt: "As you know we are confidentially under file, and Anthropic is also under file. There is a chance they pull the cover off that confidential file in the coming weeks and become public in September. That's OK, we are running our own race," Friar said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI confidentially filed its IPO prospectus with the SEC in June and has not publicly disclosed a debut date; Anthropic has also filed confidentially.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI confidentially filed its IPO prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, but it has not publicly disclosed when it plans to debut. The company's chief rival, Anthropic, has also confidentially filed its prospectus with regulators.

key_facts.fact: Slides shown at the meeting put OpenAI's revenue run rate up 35% quarter to date, enterprise run rate up 50% quarter to date, and its AI coding and work products at 20 million weekly active users.
key_facts.excerpt: Friar shared slides showing that OpenAI's revenue run rate is up 35% quarter to date, its enterprise revenue run rate is up 50% quarter to date, and that its AI coding and work product tools have reached 20 million weekly active users.

key_facts.fact: The March 2026 round of $122 billion left OpenAI at an $852 billion post-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2026, the company closed a $122 billion funding round, landing at a post-money valuation of $852 billion.

stories.headline: OpenAI previews 'Private Safety Processing', betting against Anthropic's 30-day data retention

key_facts.fact: OpenAI set out the position on Wednesday in a post titled 'Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models', previewing a system called Private Safety Processing that hunts for misuse across several related interactions at once.
key_facts.excerpt: The company set out the position on Wednesday in a post titled "Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models". In it, it previewed Private Safety Processing. The system looks for misuse across several related interactions at once, and OpenAI says its own staff never see the prompts or responses underneath.

key_facts.fact: Under the design, customer content stays either on infrastructure the customer controls or on OpenAI infrastructure encrypted with customer-held keys, with OpenAI receiving only narrow safety signals.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the proposed system, customer content remains either on infrastructure controlled by the customer or on OpenAI systems encrypted with customer-controlled keys... OpenAI receives only narrowly defined safety signals that can help identify misuse patterns.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's post takes an unnamed swipe at Anthropic: 'Some recent frontier-model deployments have required customers to allow their AI provider to retain sensitive content for safety monitoring.'
key_facts.excerpt: The post names no rival, but it describes one. "Some recent frontier-model deployments have required customers to allow their AI provider to retain sensitive content for safety monitoring," OpenAI wrote.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic went the other way a week earlier, requiring 30-day data retention for business customers on its most capable models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and conceding the policy would be unpopular.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic... recently announced that business customers using its most advanced models, including Fable 5 and Mythos 5, will be subject to a 30-day data retention policy... necessary to identify sophisticated threats and attacks that may span multiple requests.

key_facts.fact: Private Safety Processing is being tested with selected enterprise and API customers and does not touch consumer ChatGPT plans; a broader rollout and a technical white paper are planned for September.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has indicated that a broader rollout of Private Safety Processing and a detailed technical white paper are expected in September. The company also clarified that the system is currently aimed at eligible enterprise and API customers and does not affect consumer ChatGPT plans.

key_facts.fact: A carve-out in the announcement's footnote: OpenAI still retains images flagged as potential child sexual abuse material for manual review and reporting, even in zero-retention deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: US law requires OpenAI to report apparent child sexual abuse material. It keeps images flagged as potential CSAM for manual review and for reporting, even in zero data retention deployments, exactly as it does today.

key_facts.fact: Analysts note both labs agree abuse spans multiple requests but reach opposite conclusions, and that OpenAI's claim to catch the same attacks without logs stays unverifiable until the white paper ships.
key_facts.excerpt: Both acknowledge that sophisticated abuse spans multiple requests and that a single prompt is not the unit of analysis... OpenAI asserts it can catch comparable coordinated, multi-turn abuse while retaining nothing. Both cannot be right about the same class of threat.

Privacy vs safety? OpenAI and Anthropic take different paths

stories.headline: Callosum raises $100M seed to route AI workloads across rival chips, a European record

key_facts.fact: London-based Callosum raised $100 million in seed funding led by Atomico, with Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Callosum, a London, UK-based systems software and artificial intelligence infrastructure startup, raised $100m in Seed funding. The round was led by Atomico, with participation from Plural and DCVC, alongside the UK Sovereign AI Fund.

key_facts.fact: It is one of the largest seed rounds ever raised in Europe, and follows a $10.25 million pre-seed in February; Callosum has raised about $110 million since its 2025 founding.
key_facts.excerpt: Callosum, a London-based startup, has raised a $100 million seed round, one of the largest ever in Europe, led by Atomico. This follows its pre-seed round at a $10.25 million valuation led by Plural in February... Callosum has now raised approximately $110 million in funding.

key_facts.fact: Callosum says the round is the first-ever investment by the UK's £500 million Sovereign AI Fund, launched in April 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside the funding announcement, Callosum said it is the first-ever investment made by the UK Sovereign AI Fund, and that the company has also been named in the UK government's £1.1 billion AI hardware plan.

key_facts.fact: Its software breaks an AI workload into subtasks and dispatches each to whichever model and chip fits best, claiming twice the accuracy, seven times the speed and four times lower cost than uniform hardware on complex tasks, though it has not published benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: It claims that its solution is twice as accurate, seven times faster, and four times cheaper for complex tasks compared with using uniform hardware, even though it has not made the technical benchmark figures available.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the round it launched Tailored Inference, an enterprise API family offering task decomposition, multi-agent coordination and sovereign deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Concurrent with the round, the company launched Tailored Inference, an enterprise API family delivering automated task decomposition, persistent multi-agent coordination, and sovereign deployment capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The company, founded in 2025 by Jascha Achterberg and Danyal Akarca, has partnerships with Cerebras for low-latency inference and with Korean chipmaker Rebellions.
key_facts.excerpt: Its key partnership with Cerebras focuses on achieving low-latency inference at scale, and it is also entering into a collaboration with the Korean chipmaker Rebellions.

key_facts.fact: UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan said success in the AI race 'will depend not just on having access to those chips, but on using them as efficiently as possible'.
key_facts.excerpt: Kanishka Narayan, the UK's minister for artificial intelligence, tied the investment to national chip strategy: "AI is nothing without the chips that underpin it... success will depend not just on having access to those chips, but on using them as efficiently as possible."

stories.headline: Google gives college students a free year of Gemini and adds 3D study simulations

key_facts.fact: Google announced on August 19 that eligible college students worldwide get one year of a Google AI plan at no cost, plus new study tools rolling out the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: We're offering one year of a Google AI plan free of charge for eligible college students around the world — plus new and enhanced study tools — so students can make the most of this school year.

key_facts.fact: US students get Google AI Pro, normally $19.99 a month, with higher Gemini limits, 5TB of storage and access to Gemini Spark; students in over 100 other markets get AI Plus with Gemini Omni and 400GB.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is giving eligible college students in the U.S. an opportunity to utilize AI tools... with 12 months of Google AI Pro for free. Normally, $19.99 a month, the plan comes with higher Gemini usage limits... 5TB of storage and access to tools such as Gemini Spark.

key_facts.fact: A new student hub inside the Gemini app gathers study notebooks, flashcards and practice quizzes in one place, rolling out on mobile and web.
key_facts.excerpt: New in the Gemini app, we've built a dedicated hub to get you started with all of Gemini's tools and offers, just for students. The hub helps keep you organized; start a study notebook, create flashcards, take a practice quiz and more.

key_facts.fact: Gemini can now generate functional interactive 3D simulations in its answers — asking 'show me how DNA works in 3D' returns a structure the user can rotate and zoom.
key_facts.excerpt: With interactive visualizations, Gemini can generate functional 3D simulations to help you better understand the topic you're asking about... ask about a topic that could be explained visually, like "show me how DNA works in 3D," and you'll be able to interactively rotate and zoom into a 3D DNA structure.

key_facts.fact: Study notebooks will soon pull exam and assignment dates from an uploaded syllabus into Google Calendar with permission, and add graphs and images to lessons.
key_facts.excerpt: In the coming weeks, study notebooks will be even more helpful with graphs and images as part of your lessons. And so you never miss a deadline, Gemini will even schedule your key dates (like exams and assignment due dates) in Google Calendar from your syllabus — with your permission.

key_facts.fact: Google Search also gets custom practice quizzes for standardized tests like the SAT, GRE, LSAT and MCAT, plus step-by-step coaching through Lens.
key_facts.excerpt: Now, the company is expanding that initiative by baking custom practice quizzes right into Search for standardized tests like the SAT, GRE, LSAT, and MCAT. You can even snap a photo of a complicated problem using Lens, and the AI will coach you through the tough concepts step-by-step.

key_facts.fact: The launch lands as OpenAI pushes ChatGPT for Teens, with Google betting on the opposite approach of maximum access.
key_facts.excerpt: While OpenAI recently launched ChatGPT for Teens to woo younger users with homework help, Google is throwing its own massive back-to-school party tailored for higher education.

stories.headline: SK hynix and its union strike a tentative deal: 6.3% raise, 60% of profit-sharing paid in stock

key_facts.fact: SK hynix and its labor union reached a tentative 2026 wage and collective bargaining agreement including a 6.3% pay raise, disclosed to union delegates on August 20, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix and its labor union have reportedly reached a tentative agreement on this year's wage and collective bargaining deal that includes a 6.3 percent pay raise and a revised bonus scheme

key_facts.fact: Under the revised scheme, 40% of the profit-sharing bonus is paid in cash in the award year and 60% in SK hynix shares — 40% sellable that year, 20% deferred.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the revised system, 40 percent of the PS will be paid in cash in the year it is awarded, while the remaining 60 percent will be paid in SK hynix shares. Of the total bonus, shares equivalent to 40 percent will be available for sale in the same year, while shares equivalent to the remaining 20 percent will be deferred.

key_facts.fact: The change overrides a structure agreed only last year — 80% cash in the award year, 20% deferred — that both sides had locked in for 10 years, with the bonus pool funded by 10% of operating profit.
key_facts.excerpt: Under last year's agreement, SK hynix and its union agreed to remove the cap on the company's profit-sharing bonus (PS), which is funded with 10 percent of operating profit. That deal set the payment structure at 80 percent cash in the year the bonus is awarded and 20 percent deferred over two years, with the system locked in for 10 years.

key_facts.fact: On average terms, an employee would receive about 280 million won in cash and roughly 420 million won in company shares; friction is expected because payouts now move with the stock price.
key_facts.excerpt: under the new system based on the average amount, each employee would receive about 280 million won in cash and the remaining approximately 420 million won in company shares... since the amount employees actually receive may now fluctuate with the stock price, some friction is expected in the near term.

key_facts.fact: Negotiators met at the Icheon campus on August 18 and bargained into the early hours of August 19 to reach the tentative settlement; the shift toward stock was driven by shareholder opposition and social pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: On the 18th, the two sides held representative-level talks at the Icheon, Gyeonggi Province campus and continued negotiations until early on the 19th to reach a settlement for this year's wage and collective bargaining agreement... the shift from all-cash payments to partial stock compensation is said to have been driven by shareholder opposition and social pressure.

key_facts.fact: The deal still needs a union delegates' vote to be finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: The union is expected to hold a delegates' vote soon to finalize the agreement.

stories.headline: China is throttling germanium and quartz exports to Taiwan, squeezing chip and optics suppliers

key_facts.fact: Nikkei Asia reported on August 20, 2026 that China is restricting or delaying exports to Taiwan of key aerospace and optical materials, creating supply-chain bottlenecks.
key_facts.excerpt: TAIPEI -- China is restricting or delaying exports of key aerospace and optical materials to Taiwan, creating painful supply chain bottlenecks for industries in the key Asian tech economy, Nikkei Asia has learned.

key_facts.fact: The affected inputs are germanium- and quartz-based materials plus some magnets, including neodymium magnets, held up at Chinese customs since 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: China has reportedly delayed customs clearance for critical materials — including germanium, quartz-based materials and neodymium magnets — since 2025, lengthening delivery times for Taiwanese aerospace and optical suppliers

key_facts.fact: A Taiwanese semiconductor equipment maker said lead times for its products stretched by several months because of the quartz restrictions, and that no alternative supply exists outside China.
key_facts.excerpt: The head of a company that manufactures equipment for the semiconductor industry told Nikkei Asia that the lead time for its products has increased by several months due to China's restrictions on quartz supplies... "The quality and precision requirements for quartz in the semiconductor industry are very strict, and at this time we have no alternative source of supply outside of China"

key_facts.fact: An optical-industry executive said lengthy Chinese customs inspections have hit the whole industry and could significantly stretch order fulfilment times.
key_facts.excerpt: "This is a problem for the entire industry. Many of my colleagues have faced the same issue, and it could significantly increase order fulfillment times in our business," an executive from the optical industry told Nikkei Asia.

key_facts.fact: China tightened dual-use export controls on gallium, germanium and other materials at the end of 2024, causing a severe global germanium shortage; in early 2026 it banned dual-use exports to Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: At the end of 2024, the Department of Commerce China has tightened export controls on the supply of dual-use goods, including gallium, germanium, and other materials. These measures led to a "severe shortage" of germanium on the global market... In early 2026, China banned exports to Japan dual-use goods that can be used for military purposes.

stories.headline: Senate GOP tells AI companies data centers are sinking its Ohio seat and could spread nationwide

key_facts.fact: The National Republican Senatorial Committee sent a private memo to top AI companies warning that backlash against data centers is undermining Sen. Jon Husted's re-election bid in Ohio; Axios reported it on August 19, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Senate GOP campaign arm, in a private memo to top AI companies, warns that toxic views of U.S. data centers are killing the party's chances of holding a vital seat in Ohio.

key_facts.fact: The memo says: 'If he loses and data centers get the blame, politicians across the country will take notice — and they will not go near the next one. This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle.'
key_facts.excerpt: "If he loses and data centers get the blame, politicians across the country will take notice — and they will not go near the next one," the memo says. "This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle."

key_facts.fact: Democrat Sherrod Brown has spent millions on ads calling Husted 'the face of data centers in Ohio', and the NRSC says Brown has made data centers his 'de facto opponent'.
key_facts.excerpt: Husted's opponent in Ohio, former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D), has spent millions of dollars on a summer ad campaign calling Husted "the face of data centers in Ohio."... The NRSC memo says Brown has made data centers his "de facto opponent."

key_facts.fact: The memo, dated August 18, argues it is up to AI companies to fix perceptions by explaining 'who benefits, who pays, and why a community should want one'.
key_facts.excerpt: The National Republican Senatorial Committee issued a memo to AI companies Aug. 18 that paints Ohio as a potential cautionary tale... The memo urges tech companies to "fix" the perception of data centers in Ohio and show how they can benefit communities.

key_facts.fact: A Fox News poll found 65% of Ohio registered voters opposed an AI data center in their area versus 32% in favor, with opposition at 72% of Democrats, 64% of independents and 59% of Republicans; the same poll had Brown leading 53%-45%.
key_facts.excerpt: A Fox News poll found 65% of registered voters in Ohio opposed having an AI data center built in their area, compared with 32% who supported one. Opposition crossed party lines, including 72% of Democrats, 64% of independents and 59% of Republicans. The same poll found Brown leading Husted 53% to 45%.

key_facts.fact: Ohio hosts more than 200 existing or in-development data centers, and American Electric Power said Meta, Amazon and others will contribute more than $18 million to help Ohioans with electric bills that surged on data center demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Ohio is home to more than 200 existing or in-development data centers, according to Data Center Map... To temper the opposition, American Electric Power announced that Meta, Amazon and other companies will give more than $18 million to help Ohioans afford electric bills that have surged due to data center demand.

stories.headline: Merck and Moderna's personalized mRNA cancer vaccine wins first Phase 3; Moderna soars 160%

key_facts.fact: Merck and Moderna said on Wednesday, Aug 19, that intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157) plus Keytruda met the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival in the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial in completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma.
key_facts.excerpt: The study met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), marking the first positive Phase 3 readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy and for an mRNA-based cancer therapy.

key_facts.fact: It is the first positive late-stage result for an mRNA cancer vaccine, and the first to show benefit from adding one to standard immunotherapy; Moderna shares surged as much as 160%.
key_facts.excerpt: a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of recurrence and spread of melanoma in a late-stage trial, a major success in a new field of cancer treatment that sent Moderna's shares surging as much as 160%.

key_facts.fact: The trial enrolled more than 1,100 patients with higher-risk or advanced melanoma whose detectable cancer had been surgically removed; the combination beat Keytruda alone and also cut the risk of distant metastasis.
key_facts.excerpt: The mRNA-based shot in combination with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda met key goals in the Phase 3 trial in more than 1,100 patients with higher-risk or advanced melanoma whose detectable cancer had been completely removed through surgery.

key_facts.fact: Specific numbers were not disclosed and the trial continues to measure overall survival; the companies plan to present data at an international medical meeting and talk to regulators.
key_facts.excerpt: Specific data were not disclosed and the trial will continue to measure overall survival, which can take a long time to answer.

key_facts.fact: Merck Research Laboratories president Dean Li said the companies will likely start talking to regulators about the treatment 'in the next few months'.
key_facts.excerpt: The drugmakers will likely start talking to regulatory agencies about the treatment and its safety "in the next few months," Dr. Dean Li, president of Merck Research Laboratories, told "Squawk Box."

key_facts.fact: In the earlier Phase 2b study of 157 patients, the vaccine cut the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 49% at five years.
key_facts.excerpt: In a 157-patient trial, randomized at a 2-to-1 ratio, the therapeutic vaccine reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 49%.

stories.headline: Bessent doubles long-bond buybacks after 30-year Treasury yield hits a 19-year high

key_facts.fact: The U.S. Treasury said on Aug 19 it is increasing, by at least double, the size of liquidity support buyback operations for 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year nominal coupon securities, from a maximum $2 billion per operation to at least $4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The current maximum size of $2 billion per operation will be at least $4 billion per operation. This change is effective September 9, 2026 and will be in effect for the remainder of this refunding quarter (through November 4, 2026).

key_facts.fact: The move came a day after the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007, and adds at least $14 billion of buybacks in the current quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury increases buyback sizes a day after 30-year bond yield hits 19-year high... Buybacks to increase by at least $14 billion in current quarter, tiny gain compared to debt outstanding

key_facts.fact: Yields fell on the announcement: the 10-year note closed down 5.7 basis points at 4.647% and the 30-year bond fell 9 basis points to 5.196%.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark 10-year note closed down 5.7 basis points to 4.647% and the 30-year "long" bond tumbled 9 basis point to 5.196%.

key_facts.fact: Since the Iran war began the 10-year yield has risen nearly 70 basis points, topping out at 4.74% and pushing 30-year mortgage rates to about 6.75%.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the outbreak of the Iran war, the 10-year yield has risen by nearly 70 basis points, topping out recently at 4.74% and pushing up 30-year mortgage rates to around 6.75%.

key_facts.fact: Critics say funding the buybacks with more short-term bills manipulates the yield curve, could fuel inflation and pressures the Fed to back fiscal policy; debt held by the public stands at $32.2 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: But doing so risks accelerating inflation while making the cost of financing the $32.2 trillion in debt held by the public more sensitive to potential interest-rate increases, bond traders and economists said.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield had topped 4.70% before falling back to 4.65% on Wednesday; analysts are skeptical the relief will last.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year Treasury yield... topped 4.70%, before falling back to 4.65% Wednesday... some analysts are skeptical the impact will last.

stories.headline: Fed minutes show many officials ready to hike rates if inflation doesn't fall

key_facts.fact: Minutes of the July 28-29 FOMC meeting, released Aug 19, said 'many participants assessed that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline'.
key_facts.excerpt: In support of the Committee's dual-mandate goals, nine members agreed to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent... Three members voted against the decision to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate, preferring an increase of 25 basis points in the target range at this meeting.

key_facts.fact: The FOMC voted 9-3 to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, with Dallas's Lorie Logan, Cleveland's Beth Hammack and Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike.
key_facts.excerpt: The FOMC voted 9-3 in July to hold the benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.5% to 3.75%. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari dissented in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.

key_facts.fact: There was no mention of support for a rate cut; officials said the re-escalation of the Iran war 'clouded the inflation outlook'.
key_facts.excerpt: There was no mention in the minutes of support for a rate cut, a sign of how the Fed's policy debate has shifted over the course of a year that began with an expectation that the central bank would be able to lower borrowing costs this year.

key_facts.fact: Chair Kevin Warsh floated cutting the Fed's meeting calendar from eight to six meetings a year, 'held roughly every two months'.
key_facts.excerpt: Warsh "observed" that reducing the current meeting schedule from eight per year to six, "held roughly every two months" might be productive.

key_facts.fact: Since the meeting, payrolls fell by 23,000 in July while unemployment dropped to 4.1% on a shrinking labor force; fed funds futures on Aug 19 implied about a 36% chance of a September hike, down from over 70% at the end of July.

key_facts.fact: Trump wrote on Truth Social on Aug 19 that the US is launching 'the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY', warning other nations of severe financial consequences if they give Tehran a lifeline.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump has announced a "crushing economic operation" against Iran over its failure to reach a deal with Washington, warning other nations of severe financial consequences if they provide Tehran a lifeline.

key_facts.excerpt: The United Arab Emirates has imposed an indefinite trade embargo on Iran after accusing Iranian forces of firing two ballistic missiles at the country, an allegation Tehran denies.

key_facts.fact: Dubai had quietly become Iran's most important trading partner, supplying roughly a third of everything Iran imports each year, ahead of China and Turkey.

stories.headline: FDA clears two rare-disease drugs in a day: Regeneron's Pasatru and an Ultragenyx gene therapy

key_facts.fact: On Aug 19 the FDA approved Regeneron's Pasatru (garetosmab-grts) to reduce new heterotopic ossification lesions and clinician-assessed flare-ups in adults with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, a disease in which soft tissue turns to bone.
key_facts.excerpt: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted approval for Pasatru (garetosmab-grts) to reduce formation of new heterotopic ossification (HO) lesions and clinician-assessed flare-ups in adults with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 OPTIMA trial in 63 adults, the 10 mg/kg and 3 mg/kg doses cut new bone lesions at 56 weeks by 90% (2 vs 19) and 94% (1 vs 19) versus placebo; the high dose cut clinician-assessed flare-ups by 88%.
key_facts.excerpt: demonstrating a 90% (2 lesions vs. 19 lesions) and 94% (1 lesion vs. 19 lesions) reduction, respectively, as assessed by computed tomography (CT) scan. The number of clinician-assessed flare-ups... were 9 for Pasatru 10 mg/kg (88% reduction compared to placebo)

key_facts.fact: The drug took more than 10 years to develop and was shelved in late 2020 after five of 44 patients in an earlier trial died; the Phase 3 reported no deaths or serious bleeding events. It will reach roughly 220 adult FOP patients in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Pasatru was slated for FDA filing in 2021 after delivering promising phase 2 results but stalled out due to concerning safety data in late 2020. Five of the 44 patients in the drug's trial at the time died... The approval will make Pasatru available to the roughly 220 adult FOP patients in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: Also on Aug 19, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Ultragenyx's GENGLYCOS (pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr, DTX401) for patients aged eight and older with glycogen storage disease type Ia — the first treatment aimed at the underlying cause of the disease and Ultragenyx's first gene therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: Ultragenyx Announces U.S. FDA Approval of GENGLYCOS Gene Therapy, the First-Ever FDA-Approved Treatment Designed to Treat the Underlying Cause of Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia (GSDIa)... GENGLYCOS is the first gene therapy approval, and fifth FDA approval overall, for the company

key_facts.fact: The Ultragenyx approval rests on the 48-week Phase 3 GlucoGene study in 46 participants, which showed a reduction in daily cornstarch requirements versus placebo (p<0.001); continued approval depends on confirmatory data, including a 10-year disease monitoring program.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval of GENGLYCOS is based on positive data from the 48-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 GlucoGene study which treated 46 participants aged eight years and older with DTX401... or placebo, showing a reduction in the cornstarch requirements in the treated group (p<0.001).

stories.headline: Study finds 152 Polymarket wallets likely traded on US military secrets, winning 97.2% of bets

key_facts.fact: Research published Thursday, Aug 20 by the nonprofit Anti-Corruption Data Collective found more than 150 wallets on Polymarket International that may have traded on inside US military information.
key_facts.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Aug 20 (Reuters) - More than 150 wallets on Polymarket International may have traded on inside U.S. military information, attracting copycat bets and raising concerns that the market could broadcast signals exploitable by foreign adversaries, according to research published on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: ACDC analyzed all markets settled through May 5, defining 'long-shot' bets as at least $2,500 placed within an hour on an outcome with odds of 35% or less, and found 556 wallets it called 'Orcas'.
key_facts.excerpt: ACDC analyzed all settled markets through May 5 to identify "long-shot" bets, which it defines as wagers of at least $2,500 placed cumulatively in an hour or less on an outcome with odds of 35% or less. Within that universe, ACDC found 556 wallets it dubbed "Orcas".

key_facts.fact: Of those, 152 wallets betting on military and defense markets made $8 million collectively with an average win rate of 97.2%; long-shot bets on military markets won about 52% of the time.
key_facts.excerpt: Of those, there were 152 exceptionally successful wallets that bet on military and defense markets, making $8 million collectively, with an average win rate of 97.2%.

key_facts.fact: ACDC found the insider-looking trades attract copycat bets: after an Orca wagered on US military action in Iran hours before the June 2025 strikes, a bot and a whale placed copycat bets of $200,000 and $100,000.
key_facts.excerpt: When an Orca bet on U.S. military action in Iran hours before the June 2025 strikes, for example, a Bot and a Whale made copycat wagers of $200,000 and $100,000, respectively.

key_facts.fact: The researchers caution the pattern does not prove wrongdoing and could reflect luck; the typical Orca opened an account, placed a large long-shot bet, cashed out and disappeared.
key_facts.excerpt: they typically opened accounts, placed large bets on low-probability outcomes, and then quickly took profits and stopped trading. This behavior is consistent with the use of insider information, though the researchers caution that the pattern does not prove wrongdoing and could also reflect luck.
